name: Bronze Age & Harappan Urbanism
description: The rise of planned urban centres across the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra river basins, characterized by baked brick architecture, standardized metrology, and maritime trade with the Persian Gulf and Mesopotamia.
subcontinentHeadline: Mature Harappan cities flourish with sophisticated civic engineering and long-distance trade.

globalContemporaries.title: Age of the Pyramid Builders
globalContemporaries.description: Pharaohs of the 4th to 6th Dynasties construct the Great Pyramids at Giza and establish centralised administration along the Nile.

globalContemporaries.title: Cuneiform Cities & Sargon's Empire
globalContemporaries.description: Sumerian city-states (Ur, Uruk, Lagash) flourish before Sargon of Akkad unifies Mesopotamia in history's earliest recorded territorial empire, trading with 'Meluhha' (the Indus).

globalContemporaries.title: Megalithic Architecture
globalContemporaries.description: Construction of the iconic sarsen stone circles and astronomical avenues at Stonehenge.

name: Pan-Subcontinental Unification & Dhamma
description: Founded by Chandragupta Maurya and guided by Chanakya, the Mauryan state united the greater part of the subcontinent. Under Ashoka, imperial statecraft transformed into an ethical mission inscribed across pillars and rocks.
subcontinentHeadline: Imperial administration spans from the Hindu Kush to southern Karnataka, propagating Ashokan edicts in multiple scripts.

globalContemporaries.title: The Library of Alexandria
globalContemporaries.description: Hellenistic scholars in Alexandria compile world knowledge, calculate the Earth's circumference (Eratosthenes), and establish major trade along the Red Sea.

globalContemporaries.title: The Punic Wars
globalContemporaries.description: Rome confronts Carthage in the Western Mediterranean, transitioning from an Italian regional power toward Mediterranean dominance.

globalContemporaries.title: Imperial Unification of China
globalContemporaries.description: Qin Shi Huang unifies the Warring States in 221 BCE, standardizes Chinese script and weights, and begins connecting early Great Wall fortifications.

name: Classical Age & Residential Learning
description: A celebrated epoch of Sanskrit literature, mathematical breakthroughs (Aryabhata, the concept of zero), monumental rock-cut cave art (Ajanta), and the rise of Nalanda as an international residential university.
subcontinentHeadline: Flourishing of Sanskrit scholasticism, monumental architecture, and cosmopolitan academic monasteries.

globalContemporaries.title: Fall of Rome & Justinian's Code
globalContemporaries.description: The Western Roman Empire disintegrates in 476 CE while Constantinople becomes the anchor of Byzantine legal codification and culture.

globalContemporaries.title: Golden Age of Ctesiphon
globalContemporaries.description: Shapur II and Khosrow I patronize Zoroastrian statehood, silk road commerce, and intellectual exchanges with Indian mathematicians and physicians.

globalContemporaries.title: Peak of Tikal & Calakmul
globalContemporaries.description: Mesoamerican city-states build monumental stepped pyramids, develop sophisticated vigesimal mathematics with zero, and record detailed astronomical calendars.

name: Imperial Architecture & Cultural Synthesis
description: A centralized empire renowned for administrative consolidation (mansabdari system), interfaith dialogue, manuscript illustration ateliers, and symmetrical white marble and red sandstone monuments.
subcontinentHeadline: The construction of the Taj Mahal and Shahjahanabad represents the architectural apogee of seventeenth-century court culture.

globalContemporaries.title: The Thirty Years' War & Scientific Revolution
globalContemporaries.description: Central Europe is engulfed by the Thirty Years' War (1618–1648), while Galileo Galilei publishes his landmark astronomical dialogue in 1632.

globalContemporaries.title: Imperial Transition in China
globalContemporaries.description: The late Ming dynasty experiences economic stress and peasant rebellions before the Manchu establish the Qing Dynasty in 1644.

globalContemporaries.title: The Pax Tokugawa & Sakoku
globalContemporaries.description: Shogun Tokugawa Iemitsu establishes the closed-country edicts (Sakoku), ushering in over two centuries of internal peace and urban cultural growth.

globalContemporaries.title: Sultanate under Murad IV
globalContemporaries.description: The Ottomans recapture Baghdad in 1638 and expand palace architecture, governing a multi-confessional realm spanning three continents.

name: Colonial Horizon & Freedom Struggle
description: The era of direct Crown administration, railway expansion, and mass nationalist mobilization leading to independence.
subcontinentHeadline: Subcontinent unified under imperial administration and princely treaties, met by nationwide anti-colonial resistance.

globalContemporaries.title: Industrial Expansion & Pax Britannica
globalContemporaries.description: Rapid expansion of steam rail networks, naval power, and global telegraph cables.

globalContemporaries.title: Modernization & Industrialization
globalContemporaries.description: Japan rapidly transforms into a modern constitutional and industrial power.

name: Republic of India & Scientific Horizons
description: Sovereign constitutional democracy, industrialization, digital public infrastructure, and planetary exploration.
subcontinentHeadline: A sovereign democratic republic emerges, pioneering non-alignment, green revolution, and space missions.

globalContemporaries.title: Apollo, Artemis & Space Exploration
globalContemporaries.description: Humanity lands on the Moon (1969) and later establishes international robotic lunar networks searching for polar water ice.

globalContemporaries.title: The Post-War Decolonization Wave
globalContemporaries.description: Nations across Asia and Africa achieve independence, forming the Non-Aligned Movement at Bandung (1955) and reshaping international diplomacy.
